content:
Half the errors we see in Class 7 mock tests trace back to one skill. Switching cleanly between fractions and decimals. IMO setters know it — and build entire question sets around it. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Fractions and Decimals online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Fractions and Decimals in Class 7

  • All four operations on fractions and mixed numbers.
  • Multiplying and dividing decimals (watching the point).
  • "Of" problems: 3/5 of a quantity.
  • Comparing and ordering mixed sets like 0.54, 11/20, 3/5.
  • Word problems on sharing, cooking and measurement.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 2/5 = 3/4 × 5/2.
  • Multiplying by 0.1 moves the decimal point one place LEFT.
  • To compare fractions fast, cross-multiply — no LCM needed.
  • 1/8 = 0.125, 1/4 = 0.25, 3/8 = 0.375 — memorise the eighths family.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Adding numerators AND denominators (2/3 + 1/3 is 1, not 3/6).
  • Losing the decimal point when multiplying by 10, 100, 1000.
  • Cancelling across a plus sign — you can only cancel factors.

questions.q: Convert 27/5 to a mixed fraction, then find the product of its whole number part and the numerator of its fractional part.
questions.explanation: 27 ÷ 5 = 5 remainder 2, so 27/5 = 5 2/5. Whole number part = 5; numerator of the fractional part = 2. Product = 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.q: Multiply: 4/9 × 3/10. Give the answer in simplest form.
In the decimal 2.035, what is the place value of 3?
questions.explanation: The digit 3 sits in the hundredths place. Place value = 3 × 0.01 = 0.03.
6 × 5 = 30; the factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places. So 0.06 × 0.5 = 0.030 = 0.03.

questions.q: Express 0.625 as a fraction in simplest form.
Find the reciprocal of the sum of 1/4 and 1/6.
A book has 240 pages. Sam reads 3/8 of it on Monday and 1/5 of the remainder on Tuesday. How many pages are left?
questions.explanation: Monday: 240 × 3/8 = 90 pages; remainder = 150. Tuesday: 150 × 1/5 = 30 pages. Left = 240 − 90 − 30 = 120 pages.

questions.q: A rope is cut into three pieces. The first piece is 2/7 of the whole and the second is 3/8 of the remainder. If the third piece is 25 m long, find the total length of the rope.
questions.explanation: Let the total be x. First piece = 2x/7, remainder = 5x/7. Second piece = (3/8)(5x/7) = 15x/56. Third piece = x − 16x/56 − 15x/56 = 25x/56 = 25. So x = 56 m.
